changes.original: B presents one explicitly ordered life cycle in short clauses. The only printed specialist stage name, larva, is introduced as a young ladybug and repeated; pupa and aphids remain oral enrichment. Visible feeding, shedding and color changes connect each step without an unseen biological explanation.
changes.proposed: B presents an ordered life cycle in short clauses. Larva and pupa name the two visible young stages and are explained in simple language. Feeding, shedding and color changes connect the steps.

changes.original: It continues across generations. The later southward butterflies are descendants rather than the original winter butterflies making one yearly loop.
changes.proposed: Different butterflies make different parts of the yearly journey. Eggs hatch, young butterflies grow up, and later butterflies keep traveling.

changes.original: They often search differently, but methods and foods overlap: either can take food reached by the other's common method.
changes.proposed: Both birds can find some food on the surface and below it; a long bill helps the dowitcher reach deeper.

changes.original: But the battery cannot store an endless supply. If little sunlight reaches the panel, the light may not last as long.
changes.proposed: The battery stores only some energy. If little sunlight reaches the panel, the lamp may shine for a shorter time.

changes.original: Which shiny object belongs in the other tray?
changes.proposed: Which shiny object did the magnet not pull?

changes.original: Classroom table. Explicit single magic rule: one plain red bookmark follows the direction of each pencil arrow beneath it and stops on blank paper. Adjacent arrows touch so it can pass directly from one to the next. Arrows four and five initially point toward one another, making a short back-and-forth. It has no face, limbs or speech and cannot jump a blank gap. Ordinary erasing changes the route.
changes.proposed: Classroom table. Explicit single magic rule: one plain red bookmark follows the direction of each pencil arrow beneath it and stops on blank paper. Six separate arrowheads share one continuous pencil shaft, with no blank gaps or overlapping heads. Arrows four and five initially point toward one another, making a short back-and-forth. It has no face, limbs or speech and cannot jump a blank gap. Ordinary erasing changes the route.

changes.original: Six adjacent touching pencil arrows on a continuous strip; fifth initially points back toward fourth; the last arrow reaches the blank open-book page
changes.proposed: Six clearly separated arrowheads on one continuous pencil shaft; fifth initially points left toward the fourth; the last arrow reaches the blank open-book page

changes.original: Kit lays a continuous paper strip into the open book at right and draws six touching arrows. The fourth points right and the fifth points back left toward it; all remaining arrows point onward to the book. Continuity: No blank gaps between active arrows; fourth/fifth make the local trap; the final arrow leads directly to blank book paper.
changes.proposed: Kit lays a continuous paper strip into the open book at right and draws six separated arrowheads along one continuous pencil shaft. The fourth points right and the fifth points back left toward it; all remaining arrows point onward to the book. Continuity: No blank gaps between active arrows; fourth/fifth make the local trap; the final arrow leads directly to blank book paper.
